newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber lower at close in lifeless trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber lower at close in lifeless trade.

text.p: Rubber futures finished easier on Friday in light trade with traders seemingly unable to break out of the grip of a bear market, dealers said.

Local sentiment was weakened further when profit-taking pared the gains of the Tokyo market, the traders said. Tokyo's benchmark March contract, which hit an intra-day high of 136.0 yen, came off quickly and closed at 0.2 yen down at 134.3.
"There were simply no orders. It's very weak and downright quiet. That's why the entire market is so depressed," a local rubber trader said. "The fall in Tokyo did not help."
"Everybody sort of fell asleep. We're just hoping Japan has a better market next week," another dealer said.
Prices drifted in the absence of fresh buying, traders said.
November RSS3 was seen at 122.00-123.00 U.S. cents a kg at around 0945 GMT from yesterday's settlement of 123.75 cents.
November RSS1 was seen at 174.25-176.25 Singapore cents (US$1.23-$1.25) a kg from the previous 176.25 cents.
December TSR20 was seen at 172.00-174.00 Singapore cents (US$1.22-$1.23) a kg against the previous 174.25 cents.
